editorial_note: Original writing informed by community discussions about both recognisable traits and tired stereotypes. These are creative sign-level lines, not personal natal-chart readings.

one_liners: Yes, I felt the vibe change. No, I won't explain the evidence.
Tender heart, industrial-grade boundaries.
I remember how it felt, not just what happened.
Homebody, but make the inner world cinematic.
I don't hold grudges. I archive emotional documents.
Caring is my reflex. Access is still earned.
My intuition sent the screenshot before reality did.
Soft voice, hard shell, excellent memory.
I made you food because saying everything felt too loud.
Emotional does not mean fragile. Oceans are emotional too.
I am not ignoring you. I am waiting for the emotional weather report.
Everyone gets kindness. Very few get the spare key.
My shell is cute until you knock without asking.
I can tell who washed the mug with love.
Sentimental, selective, and suspicious of sudden sweetness.
I remember birthdays, tones, and exactly when the energy got weird.
My comfort show has seen things no therapist should hear.
I nurture people, not bad behaviour.
The group chat thinks I vanished. I was restoring the habitat.
I carry home with me, but the guest list stays private.
affirmations_predictions: The boundary you set will protect the bond that deserves to stay.
Your sensitivity becomes useful information when you stop treating it like a flaw.
A familiar place, person, or ritual will help you feel like yourself again.
You can remember the past without moving back into it.
A sincere apology will matter more than a perfect explanation.
Your care will be returned in a form you do not have to decode.
The next chapter asks you to trust your needs before defending them.
A home-related change brings more calm than you expect.
A memory loses its grip when you let it become a lesson instead of a location.
Your intuition is clearest after the first emotional wave passes.
Someone close will finally ask what you need rather than assume.
A domestic project brings order to more than your room.
You can offer care without becoming the emergency service for everyone you love.
The conversation ahead rewards softness with structure.
Your family story is part of you, not the limit of you.
A friendship feels safer after one awkward truth is spoken.
You will protect your peace without apologising for the locked door.
A familiar creative habit returns when you feel emotionally rested.
The next bond grows slowly enough for trust to keep up.
Your tenderness becomes strength when it chooses where to land.
micro_poems: the moon pulls at your windows,
you keep a light on softly
a laugh, a cup, a song;
your heart is not a hallway,
it has rooms and turning keys;
